Ukraine-Russia war latest: Kremlin finally speaks out on CIA director’s mysterious visit to Moscow

triage.line: CIA director reportedly visited Moscow to warn Russia against attacking NATO, after Trump broke silence on the trip.
triage.headline: CIA chief's secret Moscow trip aimed to warn Russia against NATO attack

clusters.state_of_play: The Kremlin has confirmed CIA Director John Ratcliffe's unannounced Moscow visit (via C-17 Globemaster to Vnukovo airport) — the first by a US spy chief since 2021 — involved talks with Russian intelligence counterparts, not President Putin, which the Kremlin called positive. Peskov said it is too early to say if this will improve US-Russia relations. The Wall Street Journal reports the visit's true purpose was to warn Russia against attacking NATO, following new US intelligence assessments that Putin could launch a limited assault; Trump downplayed the trip as 'semi-routine', denying it was about Iran sanctions or NATO test fears. CBS News reports the US asked Ukraine to suspend its strikes on Russia during the visit; Ukraine resumed drone attacks on Moscow hours after Ratcliffe departed, with Russian air defenses downing at least 10 drones and causing airport chaos, per Moscow Mayor Sergey Sobyanin. Separately, Bloomberg reports Russia is escalating hybrid attacks (cyber, drones, arson) against European countries supporting Ukraine, with Europe lacking a coordinated response.

clusters.state_of_play: Seven people, including two armed police officers (PC Matthew Blades and PC Tom Clough) and five young people, including a teenage joyrider who had posted TikTok videos of high-speed police chases, died when a Volkswagen Passat travelling the wrong way collided with a police vehicle on the A66 in South Bank, Teesside around 3:40am, following a police pursuit. Cleveland Police's investigation into events leading up to the crash has resulted in 17 arrests, with those arrested collectively holding 37 convictions; a separate police probe has also been launched after vehicles were seen driving the wrong way on the M6. Separately, a seven-year-old girl, Valentina Foster, and her aunt, Natalie McDonald, 34, died in a house fire in Grangetown, a mile from the A66 crash site; two men, aged 23 and 31, have been arrested on suspicion of murder, with reports suggesting the fire may be a gangland revenge attack linked to the crash.

clusters.state_of_play: Testimony has concluded in Lindsay Clancy's murder trial after the prosecution's final rebuttal witness, FBI/forensic psychiatrist Gregory Saathoff, testified he doubts she heard a voice during the killings and that she could distinguish right from wrong, noting he has treated only two postpartum psychosis cases decades ago. At a charging conference, the judge ruled the jury may convict Clancy of manslaughter instead of murder. Closing arguments are expected Thursday, with deliberations to follow. Separately, Vanity Fair journalist Brittany Romano drew backlash for smiling and winking at the courtroom livestream, and Clancy's ex-husband Patrick Clancy, now remarried, is reportedly dealing with a personal crisis and considering a move ahead of the verdict.
